newsitem.title: USA: Palestinian kills one, wounds six at Empire State bldg.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian kills one, wounds six at Empire State bldg.

text.p: A gunman who shot and killed one man and wounded six other people on the observation deck of the Empire State Building on Sunday before killing himself was identified by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani as a 69-year-old Palestinian.
His documents identified him as Ali Abu Kamal from Ramallah in the West Bank. He was born in Jaffa, Israel.
He died in Bellevue Hospital of a head wound, according to New York City Police.
"He began opening fire and shot at least eight times, hitting seven people and obviously himself," Giuliani told a news conference. The incident, he said, "created a great deal of pandemonium."

Kamal, 69, came to New York City on Christmas Eve of last year, Dec. 24, and purchased the 38-calibre pistol used in the shooting in Florida at the end of January, the mayor said. Police said the gun receipt was on his body.

The other man killed was identified as a young musician from Denmark. Among the wounded were his musician friend from Connecticut, a 52-year-old Argentine man, a 32-year-old Swiss man, a married couple from France, and a 35-year-old New York man.
During the panic following the shooting, which occurred when 350 people were on the 86th-floor observation deck, two infants and an undetermined number of others sustained minor injuries.
"It was very crowded, typical for a Sunday afternoon," Giuliani said.
He said a four-month-old boy was and a three-year-old girl were knocked to the floor. Both were in good condition.
Giuliani said a joint terrorism task force of Federal Bureau of Investigation agents and city police would investigate the shootings.
"There is no indication at this point that there is any other incident connected to the gunman," said Giuliani.
A building security camera tape was turned over to police, said Howard Rubenstein, a spokesman for the Empire State Building. He said it showed the gunman on the way up to the observation deck.
"He was wearing a long coat. The gun was not visible and presumably it was hidden under his coat," Rubenstein said.

A one-block area surrounding the building, at Fifth Avenue and 34th Street in midtown Manhattan, was blocked off as dozens of ambulances from area hospitals, police and fire trucks converged on the area. The area was reopened to traffic later in the evening.
The Empire State Building, which opened in 1931, is one of New York City's top tourist attractions, and at 1,250 feet (380 metres) high it ranked for years as the world's tallest building.

The skyscraper has been featured in hundreds of movies, including the famous climactic scene of the film classic, "King Kong," in which the giant ape clung to its side as he battled a squadron of attacking planes. The observation deck was also a romantic site for such films as "Sleepless in Seattle" and "An Affair To Remember."
